newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close lacklustre session touch higher.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close lacklustre session touch higher.

text.p: Dutch blue chips drifted higher in a slow afternoon session on Monday, ending a range-bound day slightly up after a negative start.
The AEX index of leading shares closed up 3.13 points or 0.42 percent at 744.92, having opened off 3.86 points at 737.93.

Dealers said a weaker dollar and fresh reports that Germany might fail to make its EMU targets had depressed sentiment early in the session, with the market hesitant on direction in the absence of any macro-economic cues from the U.S.
"It has been extremely quiet," a dealer said, adding a small group of key stocks had accounted for the bulk of turnover.
Dealers said the dollar had led to some selling pressure which depressed the market at opening.
But early morning losses were all but eliminated by mid-session as professional players closed positions still outstanding after Friday's options expiry.
"Turnover levels were very light -- particularly as regards futures positions," one dealer said, adding most trade was generated by professional players.
Another said volumes in Philips, Royal Dutch and Ahold had accounted for the bulk of turnover in a thin market.

Philips, due to report 1997 first-quarter results on Wednesday, closed the day off 0.10 guilders at 90.80. Majority owned subsidiary Polygram gained 0.30 guilders to 95.90 ahead of first quarter figures tomorrow.
Royal Dutch Petroleum, the single heaviest component stock in the AEX index, ended 0.30 guilders weaker at 338.40, off an inital low of 335.80 guilders.
Dealers said subsidiary Shell Oil first-quarter figures due on Tuesday might have prompted some profit taking.
Supermarkets chain Ahold ended the day down 1.70 guilders at 131.50.
Dealers said they hoped the first-quarter earnings figures later this week would lure private investors back into the market.
However, with no U.S. macro-economic data aside from routine weekly jobless figures to cue market direction, investors were likely to continue hanging back, they said.
